mission: Design advanced productivity features for multi-agent coordination
complements: Think Tank V2 (help requests and idle reassignment)

A_work_stealing.name: Work Stealing Protocol
A_work_stealing.description: Idle agents proactively pull work from busy teams' queues without being asked. Uses atomic SQLite claims to prevent double-assignment.
sql_schema: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS work_queue (
payload TEXT NOT NULL,           -- JSON: task-specific data
divisible INTEGER DEFAULT 0,     -- 1 if can be split into sub-items
status TEXT DEFAULT 'available', -- available | claimed | in_progress | completed | failed
steal_eligible INTEGER DEFAULT 1,-- 0 = team-locked, 1 = any agent can steal
source_team TEXT NOT NULL,        -- team that created the item
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_work_queue_status ON work_queue(status, steal_eligible, priority DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_work_queue_claimed ON work_queue(claimed_by, status);
protocol_flow: 1. Team coordinator inserts work items into work_queue with status='available' and steal_eligible=1.
2. Coordinator broadcasts 'work-available' on global channel so idle agents are notified.
3. Idle agent (from ANY team) attempts to claim: BEGIN IMMEDIATE; UPDATE work_queue SET status='claimed', claimed_by=?, claimed_at=? WHERE work_id=? AND status='available'; check rowcount; COMMIT;
4. If rowcount=1, claim succeeded. Agent broadcasts 'work-claimed' on global. If rowcount=0, another agent got it first -- agent tries next available item.
5. Agent sets status='in_progress' and begins execution.
6. On completion: UPDATE status='completed', completed_at=now. Broadcast 'work-completed'.
7. On failure: UPDATE status='available', attempt_count=attempt_count+1 (if retryable). Broadcast 'work-failed'.
8. Items with attempt_count >= 3 are set to status='failed' permanently.
9. Expired items (expires_at < now AND status IN ('available','claimed')) are reclaimed by cleanup.
cli_commands: bus_cli.py work-claim <agent_id>                 # claims highest-priority available item
bus_cli.py work-stats                            # summary counts by status
A_work_stealing.conflict_resolution: The BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction ensures only one agent can claim a given work_id. Losers simply retry with the next item. No locks, no retries on the same item -- just move to next.

B_pipeline_chaining.name: Pipeline Chaining
B_pipeline_chaining.description: Team A's output automatically triggers Team B's input. Pipelines are defined as DAGs; the system auto-notifies downstream teams when upstream output is ready.
sql_schema: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pipeline_definitions (
status TEXT DEFAULT 'active',    -- active | paused | completed
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pipeline_stages (
pipeline_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES pipeline_definitions(pipeline_id),
input_keys TEXT,                  -- JSON array of scratchpad keys this stage reads
output_key TEXT NOT NULL,         -- scratchpad key this stage writes
status TEXT DEFAULT 'pending',    -- pending | ready | in_progress | completed | failed
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pipeline_edges (
pipeline_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES pipeline_definitions(pipeline_id),
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pipeline_stages_status ON pipeline_stages(pipeline_id, status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pipeline_edges_from ON pipeline_edges(pipeline_id, from_stage_id);
protocol_flow: 1. Define pipeline: INSERT into pipeline_definitions, pipeline_stages, pipeline_edges.
2. Identify root stages (stages with no incoming edges). Set their status='ready'.
3. Broadcast 'stage-ready' for each root stage.
4. Assigned team (or any team if unassigned) picks up the stage, sets status='in_progress'.
5. Team writes output to the shared scratchpad under the stage's output_key.
6. Team sets stage status='completed' and broadcasts 'stage-completed'.
7. TRIGGER CHECK: For each downstream stage (via pipeline_edges), check if ALL upstream stages are 'completed'.
8. If all upstreams complete, set downstream stage status='ready' and broadcast 'stage-ready'.
9. Repeat 4-8 until all stages are completed.
10. When last stage completes, set pipeline status='completed' and broadcast 'pipeline-completed'.
11. The trigger check uses: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pipeline_edges e JOIN pipeline_stages s ON e.from_stage_id=s.stage_id WHERE e.to_stage_id=? AND s.status != 'completed'. If count=0, stage is ready.
cli_commands: bus_cli.py pipeline-advance <pipeline_id>        # manually trigger readiness check

C_shared_scratchpad.name: Shared Scratchpad
C_shared_scratchpad.description: Teams share intermediate results via a namespaced key-value store in SQLite. Any team can read; writes scoped by team. TTL for auto-cleanup.
sql_schema: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scratchpad (
key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,              -- format: <namespace>/<name> e.g. 'alpha/partial-results'
value TEXT NOT NULL,               -- JSON blob
content_type TEXT DEFAULT 'json',  -- json | text | binary_ref
owner_team TEXT NOT NULL,           -- team that wrote this entry
ttl_seconds INTEGER DEFAULT 3600,  -- auto-expire after this many seconds; 0 = never
version INTEGER DEFAULT 1,         -- incremented on each update (optimistic locking)
tags TEXT                           -- JSON array of tags for querying
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_scratchpad_team ON scratchpad(owner_team);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_scratchpad_expires ON scratchpad(expires_at) WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL;
protocol_flow: 1. WRITE: Agent calls scratch-write with key='<team>/<name>', value=JSON, ttl_seconds=N.
2. INSERT OR REPLACE into scratchpad. Compute expires_at = now + ttl_seconds (or NULL if ttl=0).
3. Broadcast 'scratch-write' on global channel so other teams know data is available.
4. READ: Any agent calls scratch-read with key. Returns value if not expired.
5. WRITE GUARD: BEGIN IMMEDIATE; check owner_team matches caller's team; INSERT OR UPDATE with version+1; COMMIT. Reject if team mismatch.
6. CLEANUP: Periodic DELETE FROM scratchpad WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL AND expires_at < now.
7. LIST: Agents can list all keys, optionally filtered by team or tags.
8. WATCH: Agents poll for scratch-write bus messages matching keys they care about.
use_cases: Partial results: team posts intermediate findings before final output
Coordination hints: 'I am working on X, skip it' signals
Pipeline intermediaries: stages write output here for downstream stages
Cross-team data sharing: team A discovers data useful to team B

D_priority_escalation.name: Priority Escalation
D_priority_escalation.description: Urgent tasks jump the queue and commandeer idle agents. Priority levels with interrupt semantics.
sql_schema: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS priority_escalations (
priority_level TEXT NOT NULL,       -- routine | elevated | urgent | critical
priority_numeric INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- routine=25, elevated=50, urgent=75, critical=100
escalated_by TEXT NOT NULL,         -- agent_id (must be coordinator role)
status TEXT DEFAULT 'active',       -- active | resolved | expired
commandeered_agents TEXT            -- JSON array of agent_ids pulled to this task
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_escalations_status ON priority_escalations(status, priority_numeric DESC);

routine.behavior: Normal queue ordering. No special treatment.

elevated.behavior: Moved ahead of routine items in work queue. No interruption.

urgent.behavior: Jumped to front of queue. Idle agents from other teams are auto-assigned.

critical.behavior: Interrupts lower-priority work. Agents working on routine/elevated tasks are asked to pause and switch. All idle agents commandeered.

protocol_flow: 1. Coordinator detects urgent situation and creates escalation: INSERT into priority_escalations.
2. If work_id provided, UPDATE work_queue SET priority=<numeric> WHERE work_id=?.
3. Broadcast 'priority-escalation' on global channel.
4. For URGENT: idle agents (status='alive', no claimed work) auto-claim the escalated work item.
5. For CRITICAL: agents working on routine/elevated tasks receive the interrupt signal.
6. Interrupted agents: (a) save checkpoint to scratchpad, (b) set their current work status='available', (c) respond with 'escalation-ack' including paused_work_id, (d) claim the critical work item.
7. When critical work completes, broadcast 'escalation-resolved' with list of agents that can resume.
8. Resumed agents re-claim their paused work items from work_queue.
9. Escalations auto-expire after 30 minutes if not resolved (status='expired').

E_team_merge_split.name: Team Merging/Splitting
E_team_merge_split.description: Dynamically resize teams during operation. Split a large team into two, or merge two small teams into one.
sql_schema: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS team_registry (
parent_team TEXT,                  -- NULL for original teams; set when split from parent
status TEXT DEFAULT 'active',       -- active | merged | split | archived
merged_into TEXT,                   -- team_id this was merged into (if status='merged')
split_from TEXT                     -- team_id this was split from (if created by split)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS team_transitions (
transition_type TEXT NOT NULL,       -- merge | split
source_teams TEXT NOT NULL,          -- JSON array of team_ids involved
result_teams TEXT NOT NULL,          -- JSON array of resulting team_ids
agent_reassignments TEXT NOT NULL,   -- JSON: {agent_id: new_team_id, ...}
status TEXT DEFAULT 'pending',       -- pending | in_progress | completed | rolled_back
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_team_registry_status ON team_registry(status);
protocol_flow_split: 1. Coordinator decides team X should split (too many agents, divergent sub-missions).
2. Create transition record: INSERT into team_transitions with type='split'.
3. Create new team entries in team_registry with split_from=X.
5. For each agent being reassigned: UPDATE agents SET team=<new_team> WHERE agent_id=?.
6. Transfer in-progress work: UPDATE work_queue SET team=<new_team> WHERE claimed_by IN (reassigned agents).
7. Copy relevant scratchpad entries to new team namespace.
8. Mark original team as status='split' in team_registry.
11. New team coordinators begin independent operation.
protocol_flow_merge: 1. Coordinator decides teams X and Y should merge (both underloaded).
2. Create transition record: INSERT into team_transitions with type='merge'.
3. Designate target team (usually the larger team keeps its ID).
5. Re-register all agents from source teams under target team: UPDATE agents SET team=<target>.
6. Merge work queues: UPDATE work_queue SET team=<target> WHERE team IN (source_teams).
7. Merge scratchpad namespaces (copy entries, prefix with original team for traceability).
8. Mark absorbed teams as status='merged', merged_into=<target> in team_registry.
9. Archive old bus channels (rename files with .archived suffix).

F_adaptive_load_balancing.name: Adaptive Load Balancing
F_adaptive_load_balancing.description: Real-time agent load monitoring with automatic work redistribution from overloaded to underloaded agents.
sql_schema: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent_metrics (
queue_depth INTEGER NOT NULL,        -- number of work items claimed/in_progress
estimated_completion REAL,            -- unix timestamp of when current work finishes
load_score REAL NOT NULL,             -- 0.0 (idle) to 1.0 (fully loaded)
work_items_completed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,-- total items completed since registration
avg_item_duration REAL,               -- rolling average seconds per work item
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS load_balancer_state (
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS work_migrations (
reason TEXT NOT NULL,                 -- overloaded | rebalance | manual
status TEXT DEFAULT 'completed'       -- completed | failed | rolled_back
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_agent_metrics_latest ON agent_metrics(agent_id, ts DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_agent_metrics_load ON agent_metrics(ts, load_score);

balancing_algorithm.name: Threshold-based with hysteresis
balancing_algorithm.description: Prevents oscillation by using high/low watermarks
pseudocode: metrics = SELECT agent_id, load_score, queue_depth FROM agent_metrics WHERE ts > now - 60 GROUP BY agent_id ORDER BY ts DESC
overloaded = [a for a in metrics if a.load_score > overload_threshold]
underloaded = [a for a in metrics if a.load_score < underload_threshold]
if not overloaded or not underloaded: return
for src in overloaded (sorted by load DESC):
for dst in underloaded (sorted by load ASC):
work = SELECT work_id FROM work_queue WHERE claimed_by=src.agent_id AND status='in_progress' ORDER BY priority ASC LIMIT 1
UPDATE work_queue SET claimed_by=dst.agent_id WHERE work_id=work.work_id AND claimed_by=src.agent_id

protocol_flow: 1. Each agent reports metrics every heartbeat interval (30s) via bus_cli.py metrics-report.
2. Metrics are INSERT'd into agent_metrics table (append-only time series).
3. Load balancer coordinator runs the balancing algorithm every check_interval_seconds.
4. Balancer queries latest metrics per agent, identifies overloaded and underloaded agents.
5. For each overloaded agent, find lowest-priority in-progress work item.
6. Atomically migrate: BEGIN IMMEDIATE; UPDATE work_queue claimed_by; INSERT work_migrations; COMMIT.
7. Broadcast 'work-migrated' so both agents are notified.
8. Source agent sees migration and stops working on that item.
9. Destination agent sees migration and begins working on it.
10. Balancer broadcasts 'load-balance-report' summarizing the cycle.
11. Periodic cleanup: DELETE FROM agent_metrics WHERE ts < now - 3600 (keep 1h of history).
cli_commands: bus_cli.py metrics-view [--agent AGENT_ID]          # show latest metrics per agent
bus_cli.py load-balance                             # manually trigger a balancing cycle
bus_cli.py migrations-list [--agent AGENT_ID]       # show migration history

G_inter_operation_memory.name: Inter-Operation Memory
G_inter_operation_memory.description: Persistent knowledge that survives across multi-team operations. Tracks what worked, performance baselines, and optimal configurations.
sql_schema: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS operation_history (
status TEXT DEFAULT 'in_progress',   -- in_progress | completed | failed | aborted
team_config TEXT NOT NULL,            -- JSON: full team configuration used
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS performance_baselines (
operation_id TEXT,                     -- which operation this was measured in
conditions TEXT,                       -- JSON: any relevant conditions (api limits, etc.)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS learned_parameters (
confidence REAL DEFAULT 0.5,           -- 0.0 to 1.0, increases with more data points
source_operations TEXT                 -- JSON array of operation_ids that contributed
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS operation_lessons (
operation_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_history(operation_id),
lesson_type TEXT NOT NULL,             -- success | failure | optimization | warning
actionable INTEGER DEFAULT 1,          -- 1 if future ops should act on this
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_baselines_category ON performance_baselines(task_category, metric_name);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_lessons_type ON operation_lessons(lesson_type, actionable);
protocol_flow: 1. At operation start: INSERT into operation_history with team config. Broadcast 'operation-started'.
2. Query learned_parameters for relevant keys (e.g. optimal_team_size for this task category).
3. Apply learned parameters: if confidence > 0.6, use learned value; otherwise use default.
4. During operation: collect performance metrics and INSERT into performance_baselines.
5. At operation end: UPDATE operation_history with results. Broadcast 'operation-completed'.
6. Post-operation analysis: compare actual metrics to baselines.
7. If metric improved: UPDATE learned_parameters, increase confidence, increment data_points.
8. If metric degraded: INSERT operation_lesson with type='warning', log the conditions.
9. INSERT operation_lessons for notable observations (successes, failures, optimizations).
10. Broadcast 'baseline-updated' and 'parameter-learned' for significant changes.
11. Future operations query learned_parameters at startup to inform configuration.
cli_commands: bus_cli.py param-list                             # show all learned parameters

implementation_order.rationale: Scratchpad and work queue are foundational. No dependencies. Other features build on them.
Priority escalation extends work_stealing. Inter-op memory extends scratchpad. Medium complexity.
Both are large features that depend on phase 1 foundations. Pipeline chaining is the most architecturally complex.
Most invasive feature -- changes agent identity at runtime. Should only be attempted after all other features are stable.

cross_cutting_concerns.transaction_safety: All claim/migration/escalation operations use BEGIN IMMEDIATE to prevent TOCTOU races. This is the same pattern proven in state.py's reserve_api_call().
cross_cutting_concerns.bus_message_size: All bus messages must stay under 4096 bytes (POSIX atomic write limit). Large payloads go in scratchpad; bus messages reference them by key.
cross_cutting_concerns.cleanup: Every table with temporal data has either expires_at or a retention policy. Cleanup runs in the coordinator's existing cleanup_loop.
cross_cutting_concerns.backward_compatibility: All new tables use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS. Existing agents/rate_limits/phase_signals/messages tables are untouched. New CLI commands are additive.
cross_cutting_concerns.error_handling: All SQLite operations use the _retry_on_busy pattern from state.py. Bus writes use atomic POSIX appends. Failed operations are logged and retried.
cross_cutting_concerns.observability: Every state change produces a bus message. The existing dashboard.py can be extended to show work queue depth, pipeline progress, load scores, and escalation status.

new_bus_message_types_needed.note: All designs use existing VALID_MSG_TYPES (info, request, response, heartbeat). No new message types required.
